group.title: More action words
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: To receive something or go and bring it.
examples: I {got} a card from my aunt.
wrong: I got a letter, so nobody gave me anything.

words.meaning: To give words or news to a person.
wrong: She told me the story without saying a word.

words.meaning: To say words to someone and have a chat.
examples: We {talk} on the phone every day.
wrong: The two friends talked for an hour in total silence.

words.meaning: To not move or not do something any more.
wrong: The car stopped, so it went faster down the road.

words.meaning: To do the first part of something.
wrong: The class began at nine, when it was all over.

words.meaning: To let someone look at something.
wrong: He showed me his photo but kept it hidden in his bag.

words.meaning: To do a job with a thing.
wrong: She used a cup to cut the bread.

words.meaning: To go down to the ground by accident.
wrong: The ball fell up into the sky.

words.meaning: To touch something hard and fast.
examples: He {hit} the ball with a bat.
wrong: She hit the door very softly, so it made no sound.

words.meaning: To take the dirt off something.
wrong: He cleaned the floor by putting mud on it.

words.meaning: To put food in your mouth to know what it is like.
wrong: I tasted the song with my ears.

words.meaning: To have water come from your eyes because you are sad or hurt.
examples: The baby {cries} when she is hungry.
wrong: He was so happy at the party that he cried all night from pain.

words.meaning: To let a drink fall out of a cup by mistake.
wrong: He spilled his juice, so every drop stayed in the glass.

words.meaning: To not like something at all.
wrong: I hate chocolate, so I eat it every day with joy.

words.meaning: To say something very loudly.
wrong: He shouted so quietly that nobody heard.

words.meaning: To cut into something with your teeth.
wrong: She bit the apple with her fingers.

words.meaning: To push air out of your mouth.
examples: {Blow} out the candles on your cake!
wrong: He blew out the candles by pouring water on them.

words.meaning: To put something over another thing.
wrong: She covered the box, so everyone could see inside.

words.meaning: To make a hole in the ground.
examples: The children {dug} a hole in the sand.
wrong: He dug a hole in the sky.

words.meaning: To try to hurt someone with your body or with angry words.
wrong: The brothers fought, so they hugged and smiled all day.

words.meaning: To hit a door with your hand so people hear you.
examples: {Knock} on the door before you go in.
wrong: She knocked on the door, but she made no sound.

words.meaning: To show where something is with your finger.
examples: He {pointed} at the big red car.
wrong: She pointed at the cat with her ears.

words.meaning: To push on something with your finger.
wrong: I pressed the button without touching it.

words.meaning: To move a door or window so it is not open.
wrong: He shut the door, so the room was wide open.

words.meaning: To join two ends with a knot.
wrong: She tied her shoes with a pair of scissors.

words.meaning: To move your hand from side to side to say hello or bye.
wrong: He waved goodbye with his feet under the table.

words.meaning: To want something you may not get.
wrong: She wished for a bike, but she didn’t want one.

words.meaning: To feel pain, or to give pain to someone.
wrong: My tooth hurts, so it feels really great.

words.meaning: To close something with a key.
wrong: I locked the door, so anyone can walk in.

words.meaning: To make the sound of a bell.
wrong: The bell rang, but nobody heard any sound.

words.meaning: To stay on top of water and not go down.
examples: The little boat {floats} on the lake.
wrong: The heavy stone floated on the water like a leaf.

words.meaning: To put something up so the top is held and the rest is free.
wrong: She hung the picture on the floor under the rug.

words.meaning: To be on fire, or to hurt something with fire or heat.
wrong: The ice cube burned the paper.

words.meaning: To go into a place.
wrong: He entered the house by walking away from it.

words.meaning: To rest with your body flat, for example on a bed.
examples: I {lie} on the grass and look up.
wrong: He lay on the sofa standing up.

words.meaning: To own or hold something.
wrong: She has a car, but she doesn’t own one.

words.meaning: To carry out an action or a job.
wrong: He did the dishes by not touching them.

words.meaning: To stop sleeping, or to make someone stop sleeping.
wrong: She woke at six and slept until noon.

words.meaning: To move by turning over and over, like a ball.
wrong: The box rolled down the hill like a ball, but it never moved.

words.meaning: To see pictures and stories in your head while you sleep.
examples: Last night I {dreamed} about a big dog.
wrong: I dreamed about the sea while I was wide awake at work.
